bug_semantics: In Basic Authentication, check_request in src/basic_auth.rs returns 401 immediately when the supplied username does not equal the configured userid, and only then calls bcrypt::verify on the password. Invalid usernames therefore skip the expensive bcrypt path while valid usernames always pay that cost, producing a measurable response-time gap that lets an unauthenticated attacker enumerate valid usernames (CWE-204).
flaw_origin: The username-gated bcrypt path was first written when Basic HTTP authentication was added. abc76a8c1f19e7efe2172f8808c171cb9d2e69ad created src/basic_auth.rs with check_request wrapping bcrypt_verify inside `if credentials.0.username() == userid`, else returning UNAUTHORIZED. Later refactor e9d33ca38d1e1f04858bdafe9ba0ac2d2fe2f69e only inverted that test into an early return; it did not introduce the mechanism.

reasoning: CVE-2026-27480 / GHSA-qhp6-635j-x7r2 is a published, non-withdrawn CWE-204 timing discrepancy in SWS Basic Auth: check_request short-circuits on username mismatch and only then runs bcrypt password verification, so response time leaks whether the userid exists. The first public write of that mechanism is abc76a8c1f19e7efe2172f8808c171cb9d2e69ad, which added src/basic_auth.rs with bcrypt_verify nested under `if credentials.0.username() == userid`. Immediate parent 5528bcb9ad2d611e8517b85762722880a90ad613 has no basic_auth module, no bcrypt, and no username comparison, so the vulnerable lines are absent before the BIC. PR #55 is a two-commit feature branch whose second commit is docs-only; the merge commit a3f4258 is not a first-write. e9d33ca later rewrote the same control flow as an explicit early return and is therefore a refactor, not a BIC. The range matches the advisory: BIC is in v2.1.0+ and the constant-time bcrypt-always patch 7bf0fd4 lands in v2.41.0, not v2.40.1. AI attribution is taken only from the BIC commit object: human maintainer Jose Quintana as both author and committer, empty trailers, no bot or AI-generation markers.
